courses.title: Headphone Ear Cup
courses.objective: Build a headphone from NURBS surfaces: a revolved cup with a vent, a pipe-swept pad, a mirrored pair and a headband, then give each cup an inner skin.

steps.title: Cup profile
steps.learn: The cup is a surface of revolution, so one profile curve defines it.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ.
Fit-point spline from the rim (radius 46) over the dome to the axis.
steps.why: A revolved profile is exactly round and easy to edit.

checkpoint.expected: A dome profile from the rim to the centre line.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Revolve the cup
steps.learn: Revolve the profile 360° around its axis.
instructions: NURBS › Revolve+: axis Y, 360°.
steps.why: Revolving gives a clean, exact cup.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Vent hole
steps.learn: A small circle projected onto the top trims an acoustic vent.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch a circle, radius 7, on the XY plane.
NURBS+ › Trim: project along Z, keep outside.
steps.why: Trimming cuts a hole without changing the surface underneath.

checkpoint.expected: A round hole at the top of the cup.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Cushion path
steps.learn: The ear pad follows a circle at the cup rim.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch a circle of radius 46 on the XY plane, 1 mm up.
steps.why: A sweep needs a path: here a circle.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe the cushion
steps.learn: A pipe of constant radius along the circle gives a round pad.
instructions: NURBS › Pipe: path = pad path, radius 8 at both ends.
steps.why: Pipe is the quickest way to model a tube, ring or hose.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Turn the cup to face inward
steps.learn: Rotate cup and pad 90° about Y so they face sideways.
instructions: NURBS › Transform: rotate, axis Y, 90°, on the cup and then the pad.
steps.why: Build in the easiest orientation, then rotate into place.

checkpoint.expected: Both parts now face along X.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Move out to the side
steps.learn: Move both parts out to X = 62.
instructions: NURBS › Transform: move X 62, on the cup and the pad.
steps.why: The two ears of a headphone are about 125 mm apart.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mirror for the other ear
steps.learn: Mirror cup and pad across the centre plane.
instructions: NURBS › Transform: mirror, axis X, copy, on both parts.
steps.why: Mirrored parts are guaranteed to match.

checkpoint.expected: A matching cup and pad on the left.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Headband path
steps.learn: A smooth arch connects the two ears.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ: a spline from (−62, 0) over (0, 118) to (62, 0).
steps.why: The arch controls both the look and the fit of the headband.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Pipe the headband
steps.learn: A thin pipe along the arch is the headband.
instructions: NURBS › Pipe: radius 3.5 at both ends.
steps.why: Different radii at the ends would taper the band.

checkpoint.expected: A band joining the two cups.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Inner skin for the cups
steps.learn: Offset each cup inward by 2.2 mm to make the inner wall of a double-skinned shell.
instructions: NURBS+ › Offset: −2.2 mm, copy, on both cups.
steps.why: Two offset surfaces describe a wall. Use Thicken on an unrotated surface when you need a single solid body.

checkpoint.expected: An inner skin inside each cup.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Car Fender with Wheel Cut-out
courses.objective: Loft a fender from station curves, extend a lip, cut a wheel opening with a projected circle, check the highlights and mirror it.

steps.title: Fender stations
steps.learn: Each station is the cross-section of the fender at one position along the car: over the crown and down the side.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on YZ planes at X −60, −30, 0, 30 and 60.
Spline over the crown (Y 12) and down the side (Y 28).
steps.why: Cars are designed in sections. The crown height falls toward the ends.

checkpoint.expected: Five arching curves along the car.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the fender
steps.learn: A loft through the five stations makes the fender panel.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: pick the five stations, degree 3.
steps.why: The loft is smooth along the car and across the arch.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rebuild
steps.learn: Rebuild to an 8 × 8 net so the surface is light and even.
instructions: NURBS › Rebuild: 8 × 8, degree 3.
steps.why: A rebuilt surface is the right starting point for trimming and extending.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Extend the lip
steps.learn: Extend the lower edge downward to make the rolled lip of the fender.
instructions: NURBS+ › Extend: lower edge, 8 mm, curvature continuous.
steps.why: Curvature-continuous extension keeps the highlights flowing past the original edge.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Wheel cut-out
steps.learn: Sketch a circle on the XZ plane and trim the surface along Y.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch a circle, radius 20, centre (0, 32), on the XZ plane.
NURBS+ › Trim: project along Y, keep outside.
steps.why: A projected trim only works where the whole curve lands on the surface, so keep the circle inside the side wall.

checkpoint.expected: A round opening in the side of the fender.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Zebra check
steps.learn: Zebra stripes show highlight quality. They should flow smoothly over the crown.
instructions: NURBS+ › Zebra.
steps.why: Stripes that kink or pinch reveal a surface flaw, even when the shape looks fine.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Raise the crown
steps.learn: Change the middle station and the whole panel, the lip and the opening follow.
instructions: Double-click “Fender station 3”.
Raise the crown by 7 mm.
steps.why: Editing a section is how you sculpt a lofted surface.

checkpoint.expected: A fuller crown in the middle of the fender.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Curvature comb
steps.learn: A comb confirms that curvature stays smooth along the crown.
instructions: NURBS+ › Comb.
steps.why: Combs show where curvature changes quickly: that is where highlights break.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Thicken
steps.learn: Give the fender a 2.5 mm sheet-metal thickness. Thickening a trimmed, extended surface is the slowest step of this tutorial (about 20 seconds).
instructions: NURBS › Thicken, 2.5 mm, density 3.
steps.why: A sheet-metal fender is a thin shell of constant thickness. The solid replaces the surface.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mirror to the other side
steps.learn: Mirror the fender solid across the centre plane.
instructions: Model › Mirror: plane XZ at the origin, keep the original.
steps.why: Left and right are exact mirror images.

checkpoint.expected: A second fender on the other side.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Boat Hull: Chine & Sheer Line
courses.objective: Build a half hull from station curves: a bottom panel and a side panel that meet at the chine, then mirror and sew them into a solid.

steps.title: Bottom station curves
steps.learn: Each station is a section of the hull at one position along the boat. The bottom curve runs from the keel to the chine.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on YZ planes at X −70, −35, 0, 35 and 70.
Each is a spline from the keel (Y = 0) to the chine.
steps.why: Stations are how naval architects describe a hull.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the bottom panel
steps.learn: A loft through the stations makes one smooth bottom panel.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: pick the five bottom curves, degree 3.
steps.why: The loft is a single surface, so the bottom is fair from stern to bow.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Side station curves
steps.learn: Each side curve starts exactly where the bottom curve ends, at the chine.
instructions: Sketch on the same five YZ planes.
Start each spline at the chine point.
steps.why: Matching end points are what make a clean chine.

checkpoint.expected: Five side curves that start at the bottom curves.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the side panel
steps.learn: A second loft gives the side of the hull up to the sheer line.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: pick the five side curves, degree 3.
steps.why: The chine is where the two panels meet. It is a crisp line, not a blend.

checkpoint.expected: A side panel meeting the bottom at the chine.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Fair the surfaces
steps.learn: Rebuild both panels onto a uniform grid for clean editing.
instructions: NURBS › Rebuild: 8 × 8, degree 3, on each panel.
steps.why: Lofts through many sections produce dense nets; a rebuilt net is easier to edit.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Reshape the middle station
steps.learn: Change one station and both panels follow. Here the mid-section gets a deeper vee.
instructions: Double-click “Bottom station 3” and “Side station 3”.
Move the chine point down to 4 mm and out to Y = 36.
steps.why: Editing one curve changes the whole hull, and the chine stays attached.

checkpoint.expected: A hull with a deeper vee amidships.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mirror to the other side
steps.learn: Mirror both panels across the centre plane to complete the hull.
instructions: NURBS › Transform: mirror, axis Y, copy.
Repeat for the side panel.
steps.why: Model half, mirror the rest: it is faster and guarantees symmetry.

checkpoint.expected: A complete hull made of four panels.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the curvature
steps.learn: The comb should be smooth across each panel.
instructions: NURBS+ › Comb.
steps.why: Combs show curvature; kinks and wiggles show up immediately.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Sew into one shell
steps.learn: Sew joins the four panels at their shared edges into a single shell.
instructions: NURBS+ › Sew, tolerance 0.05, output shell, pick all four panels.
steps.why: A hull is open at the deck and the bow, so the result is a shell. A solid needs a closed boundary: add a deck and a transom to close it.

checkpoint.expected: One sewn shell. A warning about open edges at the deck is expected.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

courses.title: Aircraft Wing: Airfoil Loft, Caps and Hollow Skin
courses.objective: Loft a swept, tapered wing through four airfoil sections, cap the ends with N-sided fills, thicken the skin into a hollow shell and mirror it.

steps.title: Airfoil sections
steps.learn: A wing is defined by airfoils at stations along the span. Each section gets smaller and shifts back.
instructions: NURBS › Sketch on XZ planes at Y 0, 40, 80 and 110.
Closed spline through ten airfoil points; chords 60, 48, 34, 20 mm.
steps.why: Taper, sweep and dihedral are all encoded in where the sections sit.

checkpoint.expected: Four airfoil curves, getting smaller and shifting back.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Loft the wing
steps.learn: Lofting through the four sections makes a smooth wing skin.
instructions: NURBS › Loft: pick the four airfoils, degree 3.
steps.why: The loft interpolates the sections; the skin between them is smooth.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Rebuild the surface
steps.learn: A rebuild gives a lighter, evenly spaced control net.
instructions: NURBS › Rebuild: 10 × 8, degree 3.
steps.why: Fewer, evenly spaced points make the surface easier to edit and faster to process.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Tip cap
steps.learn: An N-sided fill closes the wing tip from the tip airfoil.
instructions: NURBS+ › N-sided: pick the tip airfoil.
steps.why: The fill patches a flat or domed surface inside any closed curve.

checkpoint.expected: A cap at the wing tip.

steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Root cap
steps.learn: The same at the root airfoil.
instructions: NURBS+ › N-sided: pick the root airfoil.
steps.why: Closing both ends gives a closed shell.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Check the surface
steps.learn: The curvature comb should flow smoothly along the span.
instructions: NURBS+ › Comb.
steps.why: Wing skins must be fair: a kink here would show up in the air flow.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Hollow skin
steps.learn: Thicken the wing skin inward to make a hollow shell with a constant wall.
instructions: NURBS › Thicken, 1.5 mm, density 4.
steps.why: A skin of constant thickness is the starting point for structure, mass and moulding.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".

steps.title: Mirror the wing
steps.learn: Mirror the solid across the XZ plane for the other wing.
instructions: Model › Mirror: plane XZ at the origin, keep the original.
steps.why: The second wing is an exact mirror image.
steps.recovery: Press Ctrl+Z, then repeat this step with exactly the values listed under "Aakar will build".
